item.research_question: Can a new half-Heusler type high-entropy alloy be synthesized to achieve simultaneous increases in Seebeck coefficient and electrical conductivity, and how does nanostructuring via ball milling duration affect its thermoelectric performance?
item.processing_route: Vacuum arc melting (VAM) followed by ball milling (BM) for 1 h (microcrystalline) or 5 h (nanocrystalline) using toluene as process control agent at 300 rpm, consolidated by Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS) at 1373 K for 5 min under 50 MPa pressure.
item.test_conditions: Thermoelectric properties measured from room temperature to 873 K; thermal diffusivity measured via laser flash technique.
key_findings: The 1 h BM-SPS (microcrystalline) sample achieved a power factor of 1.02 mWm−1K−2 at 860 K.
The 5 h BM-SPS (nanocrystalline) sample achieved a power factor of 0.57 mWm−1K−2 at 860 K.
The microcrystalline alloy exhibited a ZT of 0.144 at 860 K.
The nanocrystalline alloy exhibited a ZT of 0.047 at 860 K.
The nanocrystalline alloy showed a simultaneous increase in Seebeck coefficient (37 µV/K to 72 µV/K) and electrical conductivity (1.08 × 10^5 Sm−1 at RT) with increasing temperature.
The microcrystalline alloy showed a Seebeck coefficient increase from 60 µV/K to 120 µV/K between room temperature and 860 K.
The 5 h BM-SPS sample contained 11% TiC secondary phase, while the 1 h BM-SPS sample contained 5% TiC.
The 1 h BM-SPS sample exhibited a total thermal conductivity similar to bulk TiNiSn, whereas the nanocrystalline alloy showed an increase in thermal conductivity with temperature.
item.mechanism: The simultaneous increase in S and σ in the nanocrystalline sample is attributed to preferential scattering of majority carriers at the increased number of interfaces (varying from ~15 nm to 2 μm) in the nanocrystalline structure. The lower ZT in the nanocrystalline sample compared to the microcrystalline sample is due to the higher volume fraction of TiC and Ni3Sn4 secondary phases, which increase electrical conductivity but also significantly raise thermal conductivity, thereby reducing the overall figure of merit.
item.limitations: The formation of secondary phases (TiC and Ni3Sn4) during SPS, caused by carbon pick-up from toluene during ball milling, destabilizes the HH phase and limits the ZT value. The ZT values obtained (0.144 and 0.047) are lower than those of pure TiNiSn, although higher than TiCoSb.
item.future_work: The authors state that the effect of the high-entropy (HE) effect on thermoelectric properties is in the nascent stage of understanding and is a subject for further study.
quotes: Nanostructuring leads to simultaneous increase in S and σ with increasing temperature.
The micro (1 h BM-SPS) and nanocrystalline (5 h BM-SPS) alloys exhibited a power factor (S2σ) of 0.57 and 1.02 mWm−1K−2, respectively, at 860 K.
This opens the possibility of achieving higher power factor values.
